summary.title: Cytonn SSO Threat Model
summary.description: STRIDE threat model for the Cytonn in-house Single Sign-On system covering login, password renewal, session management, SLO, and connected applications.

data.name: SSO Portal
data.description: Laravel application handling authentication, session management, and token issuance.

threats.title: Brute force on login endpoint
threats.description: An attacker submits unlimited credential combinations against the login endpoint due to missing rate limiting.
threats.mitigation: Implement rate limiting (5 requests/15 min per account), progressive account lockout after 10 failures, CAPTCHA after 3 failures.

threats.title: Credential stuffing attack
threats.description: Attacker uses leaked credential pairs from other breaches to authenticate against the SSO portal.
threats.mitigation: Integrate HaveIBeenPwned API check on login and password reset. Enforce per-IP rate limiting. Block known malicious IPs at WAF.

threats.title: Username enumeration via error messages
threats.description: Differentiated error messages for invalid username vs wrong password allow attackers to enumerate valid accounts.
threats.mitigation: Return identical generic error message regardless of whether username or password is incorrect.

threats.title: Session replay after logout
threats.description: Laravel session cookies are not invalidated server-side on logout. A stolen cookie can be replayed days or weeks later.
threats.mitigation: Destroy server-side session record on logout. Set HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict. Enforce absolute TTL of 8 hours and idle timeout of 30 minutes.

threats.title: Session fixation attack
threats.description: Attacker fixes a known session ID before authentication to hijack the session after login.
threats.mitigation: Rotate session token on every login, MFA confirmation, and privilege change.

threats.title: Privilege escalation via session manipulation
threats.description: A low-privileged user manipulates session claims to gain admin-level access.
threats.mitigation: Enforce RBAC on every request server-side. Require MFA step-up for sensitive actions. Sign and validate session claims.

data.name: Password Renewal Endpoint
data.description: Handles password reset requests, token generation, MFA verification, and new password acceptance.

threats.title: No rate limiting on password renewal
threats.description: The password renewal endpoint accepts unlimited requests. Attackers can enumerate passwords by observing response differences.
threats.mitigation: Limit to 3 reset requests per account per hour. Return generic response regardless of whether email exists.

threats.title: Reset token reuse after first use
threats.description: Reset tokens are not invalidated after first use, allowing an attacker who intercepts the link to reuse it.
threats.mitigation: Invalidate token immediately on first use. Expire token after 15 minutes regardless of use.

threats.title: MFA bypass during password reset
threats.description: Password reset does not require MFA verification, allowing account takeover via email compromise alone.
threats.mitigation: Require TOTP or push notification confirmation before displaying new password form. Failed MFA counts against lockout threshold.

threats.title: Weak or breached new password accepted
threats.description: No password policy or breach check on the renewal endpoint allows users to set weak or previously compromised passwords.
threats.mitigation: Enforce minimum 12 characters with complexity. Check SHA-1 hash prefix against HaveIBeenPwned API. Reject breached passwords with count shown.

threats.title: Reset email reveals account existence
threats.description: Server response differs when a valid vs invalid email is submitted for reset, enabling account enumeration.
threats.mitigation: Always return the same response: 'If this email exists, you will receive a reset link.'

data.name: Single Logout
data.description: Handles logout propagation across all connected applications via back-channel and front-channel SLO.

threats.title: Orphaned sessions after logout
threats.description: Logging out of SSO clears only the portal session. Connected apps retain active sessions and continue to authenticate the user.
threats.mitigation: Implement back-channel SLO. IdP issues signed JWT logout token to all registered relying parties on logout. Each app validates and destroys mapped sessions.

threats.title: Forged logout token
threats.description: An attacker crafts a fake JWT logout token to force logout of targeted users (mass logout DoS).
threats.mitigation: Sign JWT logout tokens with RS256. Include exp and jti claims. Connected apps must verify signature against IdP public key before processing.

threats.title: SLO delivery failure goes undetected
threats.description: If back-channel logout notification fails silently, orphaned sessions persist with no alert raised.
threats.mitigation: Log SLO delivery outcome per app. Alert security team on SLO timeout or failure. Implement retry logic for failed deliveries.

data.name: Session Store / Database
data.description: Stores session records, user credentials, and audit logs.

threats.title: Session token leaked in application logs
threats.description: Session tokens or credentials inadvertently logged in application or access logs.
threats.mitigation: Sanitize all logs to strip tokens, passwords, and PII. Never log raw session IDs or credentials.

threats.title: Expired sessions not purged
threats.description: Accumulation of expired session records in the store degrades performance and increases storage attack surface.
threats.mitigation: Implement scheduled cleanup of expired session records. Enforce TTL at store level.

data.name: User (Browser)
data.description: End user accessing the SSO portal via web browser.

data.name: Attacker
data.description: External threat actor attempting unauthorized access via brute force, session replay, or token forgery.

data.name: Connected Applications
data.description: Internal applications (intranet, tools) that rely on the SSO portal for authentication.

threats.title: App trusts forged identity token
threats.description: A connected app accepts a forged or tampered identity token without verifying the IdP signature.
threats.mitigation: All connected apps must validate token signature against IdP public key (RS256). Reject tokens with invalid signature, expired exp, or mismatched aud claim.

threats.title: App grants excessive permissions from token claims
threats.description: Connected app blindly trusts role or permission claims in the token without enforcing its own access controls.
threats.mitigation: Apps must enforce least privilege independently. Do not rely solely on token claims for authorization decisions.

data.name: HaveIBeenPwned API
data.description: External API used to check password hashes against known breach databases using k-anonymity model.

data.name: Email Service
data.description: External email delivery service used for password reset links and security notifications.

data.name: MFA Provider
data.description: TOTP authenticator app or push notification provider used for multi-factor authentication.

data.name: Session read/write
data.description: SSO portal reads and writes session records to the database.

data.name: HIBP k-anonymity check
data.description: First 5 chars of SHA-1 password hash sent to HIBP API. Full hash never transmitted.

data.name: Password reset email
data.description: Single-use reset link with 128-bit token sent to registered email.

data.name: Logout trigger to SLO
data.description: User logout triggers SLO process to broadcast signed JWT logout token.

data.name: Back-channel SLO
data.description: Signed JWT logout token POSTed to connected app back-channel endpoints.

data.name: MFA verification
data.description: SSO portal sends MFA challenge to TOTP provider or push notification service.
